      About the data

      How to read the map

      Municipality color is the simple average of schools that have data, not weighted by number of learners. For level measures, it is the percentage of schools rated Proficient or Highly Proficient.

      Each assessment uses a different scale, so do not compare the colors of one assessment with another. Class breaks are taken from the data of the selected measure.

      When a municipality has incomplete data (for example, Odiongan, which only has data from Odiongan South), check the count in the popup, such as "from 19 of 50 schools".

      There are no district boundaries on the map because the division's districts do not always match municipalities. The ranking on the left is by district.

      Data notes
      • For NAT Grade 10 and Grade 12 (2023), the overall is the average of three skills (Problem Solving, Information Literacy, Critical Thinking). It was calculated for this map and is not the official BEA overall.
      • For MPS in Term 1, Grades 1 to 3 are proficiency rates and Grades 4 to 11 are MPS. They are different scales.
      • In RMA, some entries have an MPS of 0 but a level other than Not Proficient. The level is used here, not the MPS.
      • ELLNA 2026 for Concepcion, Odiongan North and San Andres is not in the files received.
      • DUNT covers Grades 7 to 10 in SY 2026. Each domain is averaged across grades, and the DUNT average is the mean of the six domains.
      • The change measure is ELLNA Numeracy 2026 minus 2024 in MPS points. It only includes schools with both years. Levels use the Proficient scale, so the two years are comparable.
      • In RMA, some secondary schools show MPS 0 in every grade. This is probably missing data, so the Priority tool ignores RMA for those schools unless you turn the option off.
      • Landslide susceptibility was redrawn from a 55 m picture of the GeoRiskPH map (MGB, 2012), so it is approximate. A school's class is the most common one within about 165 m. Higher is worse, so it has no priority list.
      • A school is called low on a measure when it is in the lowest 20% of schools with data, or Not or Low Proficient in RMA. This is a screening rule for planning, not a verdict on a school.
      Schools not on the map

      These schools have data and are included in the municipality and district averages, but they have no valid location.

      Boundaries: PSA and NAMRIA via OCHA HDX (CC BY-IGO). Data: BEA, and submissions to CID.
